decision: ACCEPTANCE-GATE CORRECTION: do not treat the pinned Oct17 two-writer test as complete proof even if GREEN: it only asserts all three final as_of_ms are equal, not that the later B writer wins; it uses threads, and empty archive, so neither cross-process idempotence nor concurrent-reader atomicity is exercised. The stricter Oct21 B-wins oracle is mandatory, plus separate multiprocessing-spawn same-observation append and reader snapshot checks. No genuinely new source-only test specification is justified. Runtime has pytest 9.0.2, so the execution blocker is absent exact-SHA repository, not missing pytest.
source_scope: runner.run_once writes latest.json, audit_latest.json, anata_latest.json with three independent atomic_write_json calls; storage.append_observations reads seen IDs then appends without a cross-process lock. These are source-derived integration risks, not independently reproduced production incidents.
